Techtronic Industries Reports Robust Growth in Latest Financial Results

Hong Kong-based Techtronic Industries Co Ltd has posted solid results in its latest financial report, reflecting continued momentum in the global machinery sector and ongoing demand for the company’s power tools and equipment. The company, which is a leading supplier of professional and consumer tools, reported revenue growth and improved profitability for the period ending March 31, 2024.

According to figures released on Thursday, Techtronic Industries Co Ltd recorded a 7.8% year-on-year increase in revenue, reaching US$4.7 billion for the quarter. Net profit rose 9.2% to US$410 million, buoyed by strong sales in North America and steady performance in European and Asia-Pacific markets.

Chief Executive Officer Jonathan Leung attributed the company’s robust performance to “continued investment in research and development, a disciplined approach to cost management, and close collaboration with our distribution partners.” Leung emphasized the company’s focus on innovation, stating, “Our customers are increasingly looking for smart, connected solutions that improve productivity and reduce downtime. Our new range of cordless power tools and battery platforms has been exceptionally well received.”

Gross margin expanded by 40 basis points to 39.5%, reflecting product mix improvements and supply chain efficiencies. The company also reported a 10% year-on-year increase in sales of lithium-ion battery-powered tools, underscoring the industry’s ongoing shift towards cordless solutions.

Industry analysts praised Techtronic Industries’ results, noting the company’s ability to navigate supply chain challenges and cost pressures that have affected other machinery manufacturers. “Techtronic’s operational discipline and sustained investment in product development are driving its outperformance relative to peers,” said Alison Chan, senior analyst at the Hong Kong Machinery Association. “We expect continued growth as global construction and renovation activity remains healthy.”

The company’s board declared an interim dividend of HK$0.82 per share, up from HK$0.75 in the same period last year. Chief Financial Officer David Wong commented, “Strong cash flow generation allows us to return value to shareholders while continuing to invest in our core capabilities.”

Looking ahead, Techtronic Industries plans to expand its regional presence, with a new logistics center slated to open in southern China later this year. Leung highlighted the importance of proximity to key markets, saying, “Our expanded footprint will enhance service levels for our customers and support our long-term growth objectives.”

The Hong Kong Machinery Federation welcomed the results as a positive signal for the sector. “Techtronic’s performance underscores the resilience and adaptability of Hong Kong’s machinery industry,” said Federation President Raymond Ho. “Their success benefits the broader supply chain and the regional economy.”
